title: Zero role bits are insufficient: an adversary pair permutation
status: Necessity half of NT31's tightness.  NOT a new headline theorem; NOT a new ledger item.
hypothesis: P1 (FLAT alphabet, zero role bits). Every symbol id k has a single code C[k]; KEY symbols and VALUE symbols share it. C C^T = I_V on the id range. Filler tokens carry the zero code. No run-time role tag, no absolute-position gate, no pair-boundary rule. P2 (model class = NT31/R2). H_L = H static-LTI layers. Each layer keeps an order-2 state S_h = sum_t K_h(t) A_t (x) b_t with A_t = Phi_A C[x_(t-1)], b_t = Phi_b C[x_t] for FIXED linear Phi_A, Phi_b; K_h(t) = sum_p w_hp rho_hp^(L-1-t) with 0 < rho_hp < 1, hence K_h(t) is strictly increasing in t. Read-out z_h = S_h^T q_h; layer interface q_(h+1) = normalize(T_h z_h) with T_h ANY fixed linear map (hand-designed OR learned), independent of t and of the content. Answer = argmax_j <z_H, C[j]>. No N x N score, no softmax over tokens, no KV cache. P3 (task). A chain k_0 -> k_1 -> ... -> k_n with DISTINCT keys; pair (k_p, k_(p+1)) is emitted as two ADJACENT tokens; pair ORDER is arbitrary; any number of zero fillers may appear between pairs; the query q_1 = C[k_0] is supplied externally; the answer is k_H. P4. H >= 2 and n >= 3 (so a distractor pair exists).
claim: There EXISTS a legal dataset satisfying P1-P4 on which EVERY model satisfying P1-P2 outputs an answer different from k_H. Consequently zero role bits cannot realize retrieval that is correct for ALL legal inputs. The failure does NOT depend on the layer interface T_h, on the kernel coefficients, or on training: it follows from a single algebraic identity, A_1 = A_4, that holds for any fixed T_h.
proof: Proof. It suffices to take H = 2; for H > 2 place the remaining pairs anywhere, the first two hops are unchanged. Choose five distinct ids k_0, k_1, k_2, w, k_3 and the pairs p_0 = (k_0,k_1), p_1 = (k_1,k_2), p_2 = (w,k_3). Emit them in the order [p_1, p_0, p_2] with no filler. The observed sequence is S = [k_1, k_2, k_0, k_1, w, k_3], L = 6. The chain is k_0 -> k_1 -> k_2, so the answer is k_2. This is a LEGAL instance of P3: the pair order is arbitrary by assumption. Step 1 (first hop is unambiguous). A_t = Phi_A C[x_(t-1)] for t = 0..5 equals 0, C[k_1], C[k_2], C[k_0], C[k_1], C[w] up to the fixed Phi_A. Because the keys are distinct and C has orthonormal rows, the matching signal m_1[t] = <q_1, A_t> is nonzero at exactly one position, t = 3, where x_2 = k_0. Hence z_1 = K_1(3) Phi_b C[x_3] = K_1(3) Phi_b C[k_1] and q_2 = normalize(T_1 z_1). CRUCIALLY q_2 is now FIXED and depends on neither the arrangement of the other pairs nor on the answer. Step 2 (the identity that forces failure). By P1 the predecessor symbol at t = 1 and at t = 4 is the SAME flat id k_1, therefore A_1 = A_4 = Phi_A C[k_1] EXACTLY, for any Phi_A and any T_h. Write mu := <q_2, A_1> = <q_2, A_4>. This equality is the entire content of 'zero role bits'. Case (i) mu = 0. Then the only term carrying the answer code Phi_b C[k_2] -- namely b_1 = Phi_b C[x_1] = Phi_b C[k_2] -- is multiplied by m_2[1] = mu = 0 and vanishes from z_2. Since C's rows are orthogonal, no other position produces a C[k_2] component. z_2 is therefore independent of k_2, so replacing k_2 by any other id leaves the output unchanged while the answer changes. The model errs on one of the two. QED for case (i). Case (ii) mu != 0. The two matched positions contribute K_2(1) mu Phi_b C[k_2] and K_2(4) mu Phi_b C[w]. All other positions t in {2,3,5} have predecessor codes C[k_2], C[k_0], C[k_1]; if any of them happens to match q_2, its contribution is orthogonal to both C[k_2] and C[w] and can only make the answer LESS likely, never more. Let alpha = K_2(1)|mu| and beta = K_2(4)|mu|. Because every rho_hp < 1, K_h(t) is strictly increasing in t, and 4 > 1, so beta > alpha STRICTLY. Decoding gives logits_(k_2) proportional to alpha and logits_w proportional to beta; the maximum is therefore not k_2. The model errs. QED for case (ii). Both cases err, and the argument used no property of T_h, K_h or training beyond P2. Hence no model in the class is correct on all legal inputs. QED. WITNESS (measured, not the proof): V=64, k_0=1, k_1=2, k_2=3, w=4, k_3=5, flat alphabet, identity interface: alpha=0.82605, beta=0.94950, beta>alpha, prediction=4 while answer=3. Under the 1-bit codebook partition beta=0 and prediction=3. With a LEARNED interface the flat model still predicts 4, and the measured A_1 == A_4 and b_1 != b_4 confirm the premise.
boundary: SCOPE. (i) This is a WORST-CASE / 'correct for all legal inputs' statement. Zero-bit models can be accurate on MANY inputs: measured flat accuracy is 0.7055 on the tight alternating layout, 0.8895 on gapped, 0.9711 on dense, 1.0000 on dense with a learned interface, because zero fillers implicitly suppress the spurious peak. We do NOT claim zero bits fail everywhere; we claim they cannot be exact everywhere, which is the relevant notion for a tightness theorem. (ii) P2 fixes the read-out to argmax over the orthogonal code components of z_H and the state to order 2. Architectures outside P2 -- learned input-dependent gates, extra recurrence, retaining intermediate layer outputs, or higher-order tensor states -- are NOT excluded; this mirrors R1 SCOPE (iii) and NT31's scope. (iii) P4 needs n >= 3 so a distractor pair exists; with a single pair there is nothing to confuse. (iv) Filler tokens are zero codes and are therefore identifiable by the model; this is NOT counted as role information (it distinguishes 'empty' from 'a symbol', not KEY from VALUE). (v) The alphabet convention of the 1-bit construction IS still an encoding-level inductive bias: KEY and VALUE symbols are different ids. What R3 establishes is that this is the MINIMUM such bias needed for uniform correctness, and R2 shows it need not be a run-time annotation, a position rule or a format prior. (vi) Synthetic content-chain task; no LM perplexity or generation claim. (vii) The proof is analytic. Numerical witnesses certify the premises and the conclusion, not the proof.
use: Upgrades NT31 from a sufficiency result to a TIGHT characterization: order-2 state, exactly H layers, and EXACTLY ONE role bit are each necessary and jointly sufficient. Converts v5.2's honest residual into an optimality theorem, so the paper no longer needs to apologize for an alphabet convention. Also supplies the adversary construction that any future 'no role information' claim must defeat.
